user_saw: An agent hook with a sub-second timeout override could run for about 40 seconds despite a configured five-second timeout.
summary: The fix makes sub-second agent hook timeout overrides inherit the configured timeout while still rounding down overrides of at least one second.
reasoning: The hook accepted positive fractions and rounded them down to zero, which the shared agent timeout resolver treated as an unlimited run budget. I checked the hook dispatch and timeout resolver at the shallow boundary and found that both already had this behavior. The older path history stopped at a missing object, so I could not verify whether the bug shipped with hook timeout overrides or arose from a later change.
